item.title: Lake Chuzenji & Kegon Falls: A Volcanic Lake Beneath Mount Nantai — Guide
item.description: Lake Chuzenji was formed roughly 20,000 years ago when an eruption of nearby Mount Nantai dammed the Daiya River, creating a scenic highland lake sitting at over 1,200 m elevation. The lake’s outflow plunges dramatically 97 m as Kegon Falls, ranked among Japan’s three great waterfalls and viewable from both an upper platform and a lower observation deck reached by elevator, offering a close-up view of the thundering water. Both sites are especially striking during autumn foliage season.
